detail:
The National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI) describes narcolepsy management built on healthy sleep habits and lifestyle changes: consistent bed and wake times, scheduled daytime naps, and avoiding alcohol and medicines that worsen daytime sleepiness. Daily exercise and maintaining a healthy weight are also part of the living-with-narcolepsy guidance the institute presents, along with attention to safety issues such as the risk of car accidents.

NHLBI notes that a clinician may prescribe medicines in several classes, including wake-promoting medicines for daytime sleepiness, medicines that improve nighttime sleep, and antidepressants used to treat cataplexy and other symptoms. Because people with narcolepsy often have other sleep-related problems, such as sleep apnea, the institute notes that a clinician may address those problems first, and that narcolepsy can only be confirmed once sleep apnea has been treated. Therapy, education, and counseling are also described as part of ongoing care.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about managing narcolepsy and its treatments.
sourceName: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
summary: NHLBI describes narcolepsy management centered on regular sleep schedules and planned naps, with prescription medicine classes for daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, and nighttime sleep, and treatment of coexisting sleep problems.
takeaways: regular sleep schedules and scheduled naps anchor management
medicine classes target sleepiness, cataplexy, and night sleep separately
never start, stop, or change medicines without your doctor
title: Narcolepsy: managing sleepiness with routines and medicines
